record.original_question: For any n ≥ 2, is there a simple orderable group of type Fn but not Fn+1 ?

evidence.quote: Question 3.4. For any n ≥ 2, is there a simple orderable group of type Fn but not Fn+1 ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A group $G$ is said to be *left-orderable* (or simply *orderable* here) if there exists a total order $\le$ on $G$ invariant under left multiplication: $g \le h$ implies $fg \le fh$ for all $f,g,h \in G$. A group $G$ is of *type $F_n$* (for a positive integer $n$) if it admits a classifying space $K(G,1)$ with finite $n$-skeleton; equivalently, there is an Eilenberg–MacLane space for $G$ with finitely many cells in each dimension up to $n$. Type $F_1$ corresponds to finite generation and type $F_2$ to finite presentability. A group is *simple* if it is nontrivial and has no proper nontrivial normal subgroups.

Question: For every integer $n \ge 2$, does there exist a group $G$ that is simultaneously simple, left-orderable, of type $F_n$, but not of type $F_{n+1}$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to be open. Finitely generated simple left-orderable groups were constructed by Hyde–Lodha and collaborators, but none are known to be finitely presentable. Recent work produced finitely presentable left-orderable "monsters" of type $F_\infty$, but those examples are not simple. As of 2025, the existence of simple left-orderable groups of prescribed finiteness type $F_n$ but not $F_{n+1}$ remains an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Finitely presented left orderable monsters
status_evidence.snippet: First examples of left-orderable monsters that are finitely presented and of type F_infinity; these examples are not simple.
status_evidence.claim: Existing finitely presentable left-orderable groups of type F_infinity are not simple, leaving the simple case open.

status_evidence.title: Finitely generated infinite simple groups of homeomorphisms of the real line
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of finitely generated simple left-orderable groups; not known to be finitely presentable.
status_evidence.claim: The simple left-orderable groups constructed so far are not known to be of type F_2.

status_evidence.title: On some algebraic and analytic properties of the finitely generated simple left orderable groups G_rho
status_evidence.snippet: Studies properties of simple left-orderable groups of Hyde-Lodha type.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature continues to study finiteness properties of simple left-orderable groups, indicating this remains an active open problem.
